algarve.overview: The Algarve's west coast is the most consistent surf zone, while the sheltered south coast suits beginners on smaller days, making it a reliable destination for all levels. Beginners flock to the mellow summer waves of Praia do Amado and Arrifana, while intermediates and experts find heavier winter swells at Tonel in Sagres. The water is cold enough for a 3/2 or 4/3 mm wetsuit, but with one coast facing south and another facing west, there is usually a spot sheltered from the wind.

amsterdam.overview: The North Sea coast is a short train ride from Amsterdam, with real cold-water surfing at beach breaks like Zandvoort and Wijk aan Zee. It relies on short-period wind swell, making it messy but fun for dedicated locals and beginners. Autumn brings the most consistent waves, while summer is often flat.

months.9: Autumn storms begin to generate better wind swell, pushing waves into the 2-4 ft range. The water is still mild after summer, so a 3/2 mm wetsuit is enough.

months.8: Summer brings smaller, less consistent swells around 2-4 ft, making it a great time for beginners at Santa Barbara. The water peaks near 74 F, needing a 2 mm shorty wetsuit.

months.5: The beginner and intermediate reef at Surfer's Beach is generally flat during the summer months. Without winter swells, rideable waves are rare. The water is a warm 79-84 F.

barcelona.overview: Barcelona is a modest, seasonal surf destination on the Mediterranean. It relies on winter storms to produce rideable waves, mostly 1-3 ft beach breaks at Barceloneta for beginners and intermediates, with occasional larger days at nearby breaks like Sitges El Cementerio. It is flat for much of the summer.

months.1: Winter storms bring the most consistent swell to this coast. Barceloneta has beginner-friendly beach breaks at 2-4 ft, while Sitges El Cementerio suits intermediates and experts. The water is 56-59°F; wear a 4/3 or 5/4 mm wetsuit.
months.12: Winter storms bring the most consistent swell to this coast. Barceloneta has beginner-friendly beach breaks at 2-4 ft, while Sitges El Cementerio suits intermediates and experts. The water is 56-59°F; wear a 4/3 or 5/4 mm wetsuit.

months.11: Winter storm patterns begin, bringing the most consistent swell of the year. Barceloneta offers beginner-friendly beach breaks at 2-4 ft, while Sitges El Cementerio works for intermediates and experts. A 4/3 mm wetsuit is required.
months.10: Autumn storms increase, bringing more consistent swell back to the Mediterranean. Barceloneta offers beginner-friendly beach breaks at 2-3 ft, and nearby breaks start working for intermediates. A 3/2 mm wetsuit is usually needed.

belfast-giants-causeway.overview: Northern Ireland's north coast offers consistent winter surf, with beginner-friendly beach breaks at Portrush and a heavier reef for experts at Black Rocks. The best swells hit from September to March. Strong rips are a hazard at Portstewart Strand.

months.1: Winter storms deliver consistent 2-5 ft waves to the north coast. Portrush East and West Strand offer forgiving beach breaks for beginners, while experts tackle the Black Rocks reef. 45-52 F, 5/4 mm hooded wetsuit with boots and gloves.

months.1: Winter swells bring 3-4 ft waves to the right-hand point at Long Caye. The water is a warm 80 F, so no wetsuit is needed, but the coral rubble bottom requires caution. Suits intermediate to expert surfers.

borneo.overview: Modest, seasonal surfing can be found at the northern tip of Sabah in Malaysian Borneo, near Kudat, about three hours from Kota Kinabalu. The sandy beach breaks at Kalampunian Beach suit beginners and longboarders, working best during the northeast monsoon. It is a fun, tropical wave rather than a destination for experienced surfers.

months.1: Strong North Atlantic swells light up the expert reefs like El Quemao with 8-12 ft faces, while intermediate and beginner beach breaks like Famara offer 3-6 ft waves. The water is about 66 F, requiring a 3/2 mm wetsuit.

months.1: Summer holds smaller 2-4 ft waves on the Atlantic side, making Kommetjie Long Beach a fun intermediate spot. False Bay water is about 66-70 F, so a 3/2 mm wetsuit is enough there; the Atlantic side is colder.

chiapas.overview: The Pacific coast of Chiapas is far from the highland tourist trail, but Puerto Arista offers punchy, uncrowded beach breaks. It suits intermediate and advanced surfers willing to hunt for shifting sandbanks, as strong undertows and closeouts are common. South swells from May to October bring the most consistent size.

months.1: Winter Shamal winds push consistent short-period swell to Sunset Beach, offering 2-4 ft waves for beginners. The water is 72-75 F, so a shorty wetsuit is enough.

edinburgh.overview: Cold, consistent winter surf and mellow summer waves can be found on the North Sea coast east of Edinburgh. Belhaven Bay in Dunbar, 45 minutes away, is a beginner-friendly beach break with local surf schools. An hour away, Pease Bay provides a punchier beach break for intermediate and advanced surfers.

fiji.overview: Fiji is home to world-reference reef breaks like Cloudbreak and Restaurants, drawing experts for heavy, hollow lefts. These waves break over shallow coral and require a boat ride from the main islands. The prime season runs from April to October when powerful swells arrive from the south. It is strictly for experienced surfers, with 77-82 F water and no wetsuit needed.

months.1: The off-season brings smaller, inconsistent waves and humid weather. Swells are less frequent in summer, though mid-sized swells still arrive on some days, offering 2-4 ft surf for those already there.

mallorca.overview: Modest, wind-driven Mediterranean surf arrives on Mallorca during the winter months. Beginners can learn on the sandy stretches of Playa de Muro and Son Serra de Marina, while experienced surfers head to Cala Mesquida when storms push swell to the north and east coasts.

months.1: Winter storms bring the most consistent windswell to the north and east coasts, producing 1-3 ft waves. Beginners find easy whitewash at Playa de Muro, while Son Serra de Marina is another gentle option, in 59 F water (4/3 mm wetsuit).
months.2: The winter swell pattern holds steady, offering 1-3 ft waves on the northern beaches. Experienced surfers can find steeper sections at Cala Mesquida when the wind aligns.
months.11: Consistency improves as winter weather sets in. Beginners head to Son Serra de Marina for 2-3 ft waves, and water temperatures drop, requiring a wetsuit.
months.12: Winter storms provide the island's most reliable surf. Playa de Muro offers gentle 1-3 ft waves for beginners, while Cala Mesquida provides steeper sections for experienced surfers.

rio.overview: Consistent beach breaks and the famous left-hand point at Arpoador define the surf in Rio de Janeiro. Barra da Tijuca and Macumba provide beginner-friendly peaks, while Arpoador suits intermediate to advanced surfers. The best swells arrive in winter, though waves break year-round.

months.4: Autumn swells increase the size to 4-6 ft. Intermediate surfers find good lefts at Arpoador, while Macumba's fat waves suit beginners. The water cools slightly to 75 F, and beginners have fun inside sections.
months.5: Winter south swells deliver consistent 6-8 ft waves. The intermediate point break at Arpoador fires with long lefts, while Macumba offers fat peaks that suit beginners on smaller days. Beginners find smaller inside sections at Barra da Tijuca. Water is 68 F, 2 mm wetsuit.
months.6: Winter south swells deliver consistent 6-8 ft waves. The intermediate point break at Arpoador fires with long lefts, while Macumba offers fat peaks that suit beginners on smaller days. Beginners find smaller inside sections at Barra da Tijuca. Water is 68 F, 2 mm wetsuit.

months.9: Swell size eases to 4-7 ft. Arpoador still provides excellent intermediate lefts, and Macumba holds fun, fat peaks. Beginners can surf the smaller days at Barra da Tijuca.

months.8: Late winter maintains the powerful swells and cold water (52-55 F). Shipstern Bluff remains the focus for big-wave experts, and Marion Bay offers strong beach break conditions.

vancouver-island.overview: Tofino on Vancouver Island is Canada's surf capital, where consistent beach breaks sit against a rugged, forested coastline. Cox Bay handles larger swells for experienced surfers, while Chesterman Beach provides gentler waves for beginners and Long Beach suits intermediates. The water is cold year-round (46-60 F, 4/3 mm wetsuit in summer, 5/4 mm hooded with boots and gloves in winter). Watch out for strong rips and drift logs in the surf.

months.6: Summer brings smaller, consistent 3-6 ft waves. Chesterman Beach is excellent for beginners, Long Beach suits intermediates, and a 4/3 mm wetsuit is usually enough.
